hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline through this pipeline before proposing anything.
rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.
note: seeds best-so-far and the convergence window; does not start the stall counter

hypothesis: Replace the pointwise FM with LightGBM trained with lambdarank on user groups capped at 6 consecutive rows, over base5 plus out-of-fold item/author aggregates and within-user duration features.
rationale: Three structural defects of the baseline are fixed at once: the loss becomes a ranking loss whose pair weights follow the NDCG gain, the training group length (6) is matched to the ~5.6-row lists actually scored so the position discount and the pair set resemble the evaluation lists, and the frame finally contains quantities that vary WITHIN a user list and are known to be predictive of long_view (video-level historical long-view rate, and duration relative to the rest of the list). An FM on five raw ids can only reorder a user's list through the item-side embedding; a tree with an OOF item long-view rate reads that same signal directly and in a monotone, low-variance form, and 99.9% valid-video coverage means the aggregate is populated almost everywhere.
expected_gain_derivation: Three separately-argued sources stack here. [POINTWISE_BASELINE] plus [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]: the organizers list loss change first as unexplored, and on ~6-item lists a listwise/pairwise loss changes the whole ordering, not just the head; comparable published pointwise->lambdarank swaps on short lists are worth ~0.01. [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH]: training on 43.5-row groups while scoring 5.6-row lists mistrains the discount; capping at 6 is worth a further ~0.005. The largest term is the feature/model change: [ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD] applies to STATIC id fields, not to outcome aggregates, and an OOF video long-view rate is the single strongest within-user discriminator available; on the 57.8% influenceable users [CEILING] there is 0.247 of headroom, so capturing a modest slice of it gives ~0.02. Total ~0.035, with real downside risk if LightGBM handles 26k-level id categoricals badly, which is why item_agg is included in the same spec rather than after it.

block_justifications.base5: The baseline's five fields are the only identity information in the frame and the organizers measured the user_id x video_id interaction as carrying most of the learnable signal, so removing them would discard the known-good core.
block_justifications.item_agg: Video/author long-view and click rates vary within a user's list and are therefore the one class of quantity that can actually reorder it [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]; they are OOF encoded as the guard requires.
block_justifications.dur_feats: Duration percentile rank is computed within the user's own list, so it is by construction non-constant per user, and duration-bias modelling is explicitly on the organizers' unexplored list [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED].

hypothesis: Adding the cross_agg block (user x author affinity, user x tag affinity, and duration relative to the user's historically long-viewed duration) to the iteration-1 LightGBM lambdarank/chunk-6 configuration will improve within-user ordering.
rationale: Every quantity in cross_agg varies across the rows of a single user's list, so unlike user-side aggregates it can actually reorder that list [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT]. It is also the only available block that touches two of the organizers' explicitly unexplored directions at once: user behaviour history (author/tag affinity built from the user's past) and duration-bias modelling relative to that user's own watched-duration profile. Iteration 1 gave the trees only item-side popularity and list-relative duration; nothing in the current frame tells the model that THIS user prefers THIS author or this length of video, and on a ~6-item list one correctly promoted item moves nDCG@5 a lot [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS].
expected_gain_derivation: Iteration 1's whole bundle (model family + loss + grouping + item_agg + dur_feats) bought only +0.0013 over the FM baseline, so I discount large feature effects heavily. Against that, [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] lists behaviour-history and duration-bias as untouched, and [CEILING] leaves 0.247 of headroom on the 57.8% influenceable users, so capturing even 3% of it is ~0.007. I shade this down rather than up because [CF_DIAGNOSTIC_DIVERGENCE] warns that user-item match features underperform specifically on the standard log (the deployed policy already pre-filtered each list for affinity, so affinity is near-saturated within a logged list); the duration-relative-to-user-history component is not an affinity match and should survive that argument, which is why I still expect net positive rather than zero. Well above [SEED_NOISE] of 0.0008 if real.

hypothesis: Strip every high-cardinality identity categorical from the frame and rank with a purely dense, within-user-varying feature set (OOF item/author rates, within-user duration features, user-item affinity) under a listwise rank_xendcg loss on 6-row groups.
rationale: Iteration 1 added a ranking loss, matched grouping and strong OOF aggregates yet moved only +0.0013 over an FM, which is the signature of the tree spending its splits on 26k-level user_id and ~7k-level video_id categoricals: with max_cat_threshold 64 a tree can only carve those into coarse arbitrary subsets, which is high-variance noise in train and near-useless in valid, and any split on user_id alone is user-constant and cannot reorder anything [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT]. Removing base5 forces all capacity onto quantities that provably vary inside a user's logged list, and item_agg is already a better-estimated, OOF version of exactly the item-identity signal video_id was carrying [HIGH_COVERAGE]. The loss is switched to rank_xendcg because half the primary is GAUC, which weights all within-user pairs equally, and on ~6-item lists nDCG@5 is essentially full-list ordering [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS], so lambdarank's position discount is a mismatch the listwise softmax does not have.
expected_gain_derivation: Two independent terms. (a) Denoising: the FM at 0.6014 gets its whole score from the user x video interaction, yet LightGBM with those ids PLUS aggregates only reached 0.60275 [ORGANIZER_CAPACITY_DEAD suggests the id interaction is saturated, so the ids are contributing variance rather than signal in a tree]; recovering that variance is worth ~0.004. (b) Objective match: GAUC is unweighted pairs and [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS] says nDCG@5 over 6 items is whole-list ordering, so dropping the NDCG position discount should add ~0.002. Total ~0.006 as a mean, but with genuinely wide spread (I would not be surprised by -0.015 if video_id carries item quality the OOF rates cannot) - this is the forced high-variance move and the bar this iteration is only best>0.6034 under [CONVERGENCE_MECHANICS].

block_justifications.item_agg: OOF video/author long-view and click rates are the strongest item-quality signal that varies inside a user's logged list, and they are the dense replacement for the video_id/author_id categoricals this spec deliberately removes [WITHIN_USER_RANKING].
block_justifications.dur_feats: Log duration and within-user duration percentile are non-constant per user by construction and carry the duration bias in long_view that the organizers left unexplored, and they replace dur_bucket from base5 [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED].
block_justifications.cross_agg: Without base5 there is no user-side information at all in the frame, and user x author / user x tag affinity plus duration-relative-to-user-history are the only remaining personalised features that vary within a list, so they are needed here to keep the model from being purely item-global.
